releases.body:
# Q-Pathformer Study v0.9 — Learned Routing and Classical Controls

Prepared for owner review as a GitHub draft. Repository edition v1.0 is separate from study v0.9.

Learned circuit routing won five, lost three and was inconclusive in four of twelve primary BCE contrasts; three wins exceeded the 0.01 practical reference throughout their adjusted intervals. G121 remained much better on checkerboard and spiral. MLP4 led the descriptive Banknote check. Exact conversion preserved 276 circuit predictors and 1,380 expert cores.

Plan B compares hard geometric routing, fixed soft mixtures, learned soft mixtures, parameter-count-matched residual controls and G121. Four synthetic families use eight confirmation populations and two paired optimizer seeds. Banknote Authentication is a secondary fixed grouped split with five optimizer seeds and additional MLP2, MLP4 and LR2 controls.

48 engineering, 72 development, 636 confirmation and four clean retraining fits. Banknote is one fixed split, not five independent datasets. Shared diagnostic numerical primitives, small-sample t assumptions, mixture costs, local timing and absent physical hardware constrain claims. releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.6 — Harder Tasks and Faster Inference
releases.body:
**Published release · Private repository · Study · Documentation · Code**

Q-Pathformer v0.6 asks whether richer circuit readouts help on harder classification boundaries, and whether the same trained circuit can run faster through an equivalent classical representation. Six recipes were compared on checkerboard, spiral, noisy annulus and rare-positive disks, using five paired training seeds on one fixed confirmation split per task family. All circuit execution used classical compute.

This completed study is presented in Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0. Study v0.6 and repository edition v1.0 are separate identifiers. The design includes **48 development and 120 confirmation endpoints**, plus 24 separate engineering endpoints.

### Historical findings

**Common clipped binary cross-entropy (BCE) was the primary endpoint; lower is better.** These are means over five confirmation training seeds. Macro-F1 is secondary.

| Recipe | Checkerboard | Spiral | Noisy annulus | Rare disks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scalar | 0.57805 | 0.50069 | 0.41064 | 0.01345 |
| Multi | 0.52162 | 0.42532 | 0.40911 | 0.01456 |
| Routed Trig25 | 0.30504 | 0.24828 | 0.40317 | 0.01487 |

Multi improves on Scalar on checkerboard and spiral, while routed Trig25 achieves lower mean common clipped BCE on both. Noisy-annulus and rare-disk results do not establish a general improvement from the richer readout. Small or unresolved differences are not equivalence results.

Checkerboard mean macro-F1 rises from **73.03% to 78.55%**, and spiral from **77.60% to 84.71%**, for Scalar to Multi. The sixteen primary contrasts use 99.6875% Bonferroni-adjusted paired-seed intervals. A separate 10,000-draw paired-record bootstrap conditions on the trained checkpoints; it does not add training replications.

Forty selected circuit checkpoints were converted to equivalent classical coefficients. The checks found no classification differences and numerical agreement within the declared tolerances. Conversion reduced measured CPU inference time. It is another representation of the same fitted predictor, not an additional trained model.

An equally optimized routed Trig25 control uses the same coefficient inference kernel and has comparable inference cost; the global MLP is faster in the displayed tables. Conversion improves the retained circuit implementation without establishing a speed advantage over equally optimized classical controls or quantum speedup.

### Historical verification and limitations

The analytical conversion applies to the retained two-layer encoding and linear Pauli-logit heads. Finite validation/test, off-grid, boundary and forced-bank checks quantify floating-point agreement, not bitwise equality for every input or arbitrary circuit families. The coefficient representation increases parameter storage; it is a time/representation tradeoff, not compression.

Deployment timings used an isolated process with one BLAS thread and no concurrent training. Hot inference includes routing, features and sigmoid, excluding loading; compilation is separate. Batch size and unexplained timing drift limit comparisons, so no universal speedup multiplier is claimed.

Historical local readiness covers **40 checkpoints and 983,040 Aer simulated shots**, with separate probability-level multinomial diagnostics. The Manila device properties are an archived 27 May 2024 snapshot, not current calibration. Release preparation does not repeat these experiments.

These are small two-dimensional synthetic binary classifiers with fixed routers and unequal capacities. Five paired training seeds on one fixed confirmation split per task family do not establish population-wide or real-world generalization. Historical prior-version scores provide context, not paired improvement evidence. No physical-QPU result, quantum advantage, ETEL implementation or full language-architecture benchmark is supplied.

releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.5 — Flexible Readouts and Classical Controls
releases.body:
**Published release · Private repository · Study · Documentation · Code**

Q-Pathformer v0.5 examines how learned output heads change shallow circuit classifiers when compared with strong classical controls. Eleven recipes were evaluated on two independently generated circle populations and a rotated ellipse, using five paired training seeds and one fixed split per confirmation population. All circuit execution used classical compute.

This completed study is presented in **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**. Study v0.5 and repository edition v1.0 are separate identifiers. All **66 development and 165 confirmation endpoints** completed **200 rounds and 15,000 optimizer updates per endpoint**, following 22 short engineering endpoints.

### Historical findings

**Common clipped binary cross-entropy (BCE) was the primary endpoint; lower is better.** These are means over five confirmation training seeds. Macro-F1 is secondary.

| Recipe | Mean common clipped BCE: circle 1 | Circle 2 | Rotated ellipse |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Legacy | 0.22279 | 0.17937 | 0.21335 |
| Scalar | 0.01362 | 0.01676 | 0.02599 |
| Multi | 0.01315 | 0.01298 | 0.02096 |
| Trig25 routed | 0.01054 | 0.01201 | 0.01399 |

The learned-readout recipes substantially improved on the same-study Legacy recipe. Scalar changes the probability link, head parameters, capacity and native training loss together, so this comparison does not isolate the readout's contribution. Five-moment Multi adds a smaller, task-dependent benefit over Scalar: both circle adjusted seed intervals include zero; the ellipse loss reduction is below the registered 0.01 practical reference. The random frozen-core control performed substantially worse.

Scalar reached mean macro-F1 of **99.06–99.54%**, and Multi reached **99.29–99.55%** across these populations. Those small F1 differences do not establish general superiority of five moments.

**Strong classical controls remain central to the result.** Routed Trig25 had the lowest mean common clipped BCE on all three confirmation populations. Its advantage over Multi was unresolved by the adjusted seed intervals on the circles and resolved on the ellipse. Trig25 controls combined high mean accuracy with much lower measured local execution time than the circuit recipes. These are measurements of the retained CPU implementations, not general hardware-efficiency or monetary-cost claims.

The twelve registered primary contrasts use **99.5833% Bonferroni-adjusted paired-seed intervals**. The separate 10,000-resample record bootstrap conditions on the trained models; it does not add training replications. These uncertainty sources remain separate.

### Historical verification and limitations

Historical independent replay checked saved states, predictions, selected checkpoints and statistics; it did not repeat every optimizer update. Local readiness covered **60 selected circuit checkpoints** and **1,474,560 simulated Aer measurement shots**. Separate conditional multinomial diagnostics are documented in the report. No physical shots or hardware jobs are reported; illustrative noise is not device calibration.

These results concern small synthetic classifiers, fixed routers and unequal capacities. The ellipse changes the label boundary under the same uniform input distribution; it is not an out-of-distribution benchmark. Five training seeds and one fixed split per population do not establish broad task or real-world generalization. Historical scores from earlier studies provide context, not paired improvement evidence. No physical-QPU result, quantum advantage, ETEL implementation or full language-model benchmark is supplied.

Reported training-loop times are elapsed wall times under concurrent CPU workers, including validation and evidence writes. They are not process CPU seconds, isolated hardware benchmarks, energy estimates or cloud costs. The 97% validation milestone was diagnostic; all runs completed their full budgets, so no early-stopping saving was measured. The report's exact learned-logit representation is a historical research direction, not deployment benchmarking of a newly compiled evaluator.

releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.4 — Routing and Circuit Contribution
releases.body:
**Published release · Private repository · Study · Documentation · Code**

Q-Pathformer v0.4 asks what shallow circuit models contribute when the same routing choices are also available to conventional models. This completed study is presented in **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**. Study v0.4 and repository edition v1.0 are separate identifiers.

The study crosses three model families with three routing policies: a **two-qubit, depth-two circuit model (Q2)**, a raw-coordinate ReLU MLP and a 25-feature trigonometric sigmoid-logit model; each is evaluated globally, with coordinate-hash routing or with training-only k-means routing. Routed examples activate one of five parameter banks. The fixed k-means router is fitted to training coordinates without labels.

All **54 development and 135 confirmation endpoints** completed **200 rounds and 15,000 optimizer updates per endpoint**. Confirmation used five training seeds for every model/population combination across two independent circle populations and a rotated ellipse. All circuit execution was simulated on classical compute.

### Historical findings

**Binary cross-entropy (BCE) was the primary metric; lower is better.** Spatial k-means routing improved Q2 over its hash-routing control on all three confirmation populations. The following values are means over five confirmation training seeds; macro-F1 is secondary.

| Q2 k-means confirmation population | Mean test BCE | Mean macro-F1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Circle population 1 | 0.17689 | 98.32% |
| Circle population 2 | 0.18280 | 97.16% |
| Rotated ellipse | 0.21207 | 94.41% |

**The classical controls remained stronger.** Global MLP and global trigonometric models achieved lower mean BCE and higher mean macro-F1 on every confirmation population. Routed trigonometric models also achieved lower BCE than routed Q2 throughout. Q2's favorable mean BCE differences against the small routed MLP remain **unresolved across training seeds**: the adjusted paired-seed intervals include zero on all three populations. This is neither equivalence nor evidence of a general circuit advantage.

The nine registered primary contrasts use **99.4444% Bonferroni-adjusted intervals**. Paired-seed intervals and the separate 5,000-resample record bootstrap describe different sources of uncertainty. The record bootstrap conditions on the trained models; it does not add training replications or resolve training instability.

### Historical verification and limitations

Historical independent replay checked **135 endpoints and 216,000 checkpoint–record predictions**. Each population has 1,600 held-out test records shared by its 45 checkpoints; the prediction count is not a count of independent test cases. Replay verifies saved states, predictions and statistics; it is not a second execution of every optimizer update.

Local readiness checks covered all **45 circuit checkpoints** and included **737,280 simulated Aer measurement shots**. Separate conditional binomial diagnostics are documented in the report; no physical shots or hardware jobs are reported. Illustrative logical-noise scenarios are not device calibration or current IBM device qualification.

Five seeds, synthetic tasks, fixed routers and unequal model capacities do not isolate a circuit-specific benefit or establish quantum advantage, speed or real-world generalization. Validation crossings of the 97% macro-F1 milestone were learning diagnostics: every run completed its full budget, so they show neither realized early-stopping savings nor held-out performance at an earlier update. Original future-study recommendations remain historical recommendations; packaging adds no experiments or completed later studies.

releases.body:
**Published release · Private repository · Study · Documentation · Code**

Q-Pathformer v0.3 examines shallow circuits, parameter sharing and routing on a synthetic circle task. This completed study is presented in **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**. Study v0.3, report edition 1 and repository edition v1.0 are separate identifiers.

The historical study completed all **104 registered training runs: 39 development and 65 confirmation**. All 13 methods continued to five-seed confirmation on fresh synthetic circle data, using the same **1,600 held-out test records**. All circuit execution was simulated on classical compute.

**Binary cross-entropy (BCE) was the primary metric; lower is better.** K-means routed depth-two circuits achieved mean BCE **0.1897**, compared with **0.2897** for hash routing using the same 40 circuit angles. The paired difference was **−0.1000**, with a Bonferroni-adjusted **98.333% seed interval of [−0.1232, −0.0769]**. releases.body:
**Published release · Private repository · Study · Documentation · Code**

Q-Pathformer v0.2 tested two design questions: whether stable text routing improves classification, and whether separate parameter banks improve small circuits that operate at different depths. This completed study is presented in **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**; the repository edition and study version are separate identifiers.

The work combines a classical GPU text experiment on **DBpedia14 title-plus-content classification** with a separate synthetic circuit experiment. All **94 registered main runs** (27 text and 67 circuit-study runs) and **eight separate common text warmups** completed. Confirmation covered 15 text endpoints and 40 circuit-study endpoints, including classical controls in the latter.

### Main findings

**Text routing:** Hash18 reached **97.659% macro-F1**, compared with **97.642%** for current content routing and **97.602%** for shared adapters. Its primary mean gain over current content routing was **0.01694 percentage points**, with paired seed t95 interval **[-0.11024, +0.14412]**. The interval includes zero; the study did not establish a resolved primary improvement.

**Circuit parameters:** Giving each depth its own parameter bank improved the selected comparison with the original shared-parameter schedule. Untied assigned circuits reached **81.44% macro-F1**, compared with **71.83%** for the shared schedule. The change increased allocated angles from **16 to 40**. The fixed four-layer circuit reached **93.32%**, and the matched-information classical **MLP129 reached 99.04%**. The primary circuit comparison used binary cross-entropy: untied assigned minus shared schedule was **-0.14441**, with paired seed t95 interval **[-0.15434, -0.13449]**; lower is better. F1 is secondary.

The text experiment used a classical GPU; the quantum circuits were simulated locally. No physical-QPU execution or quantum advantage is reported. These are separate models on separate tasks, not an integrated quantum text model. The parameter-bank comparison does not isolate a scheduling or gradient-interference benefit, and MLP129 is information-matched rather than parameter- or compute-matched.

The trained-checkpoint readiness audit used **3,686,400 simulated shots**, with **zero physical shots or hardware jobs**. **Study · Documentation · Code**

This is the first study release in **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**. Releases retain their study identifiers; the included completed allocation study is **v0.9.5**. Repository access is currently private while further study releases are prepared.

The execution component is **Q-Path Multiplier - Elastic Task Execution Layer (ETEL) v0.1**. Its incorporated source identifier remains 0.2.0. These component and repository identifiers do not renumber the study.

## Findings and reproduction

None of the eight registered comparisons established the stipulated 0.01 native-BCE improvement for the tested ETEL allocation policy. Successive halving used less mean native CPU on all four tasks. These findings concern the tested allocation policy; they do not constitute physical-QPU results. See the [study summary](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.9.5/release_notes/study-v0.9.5.md).
